## Basic workflow

```
scripts/install-fork.sh
grok-fork traces
```

`scripts/install-fork.sh` is the build-and-install protocol (Sab, 2026-11-11: grok-traces ships with grok-fork every time). One cargo run builds both `xai-grok-pager-bin` and `xai-grok-traces`; it copies `grok-fork` and `grok-traces` into `~/.grok/bin` on this Mac and on sab-air (`GROK_FORK_REMOTE`, default `sab-mini@sab-air`) by copy-then-rename, and exits non-zero unless all four checksums match the build. `--no-build` installs what `target/release` holds, for when the build already ran in its own tab.

The standalone command opens the Traces list directly. Alternatively, run `grok-fork` and type `/traces` in the prompt.

## List keys (2026-11-11)

- `/` searches the list (title, folder, model, id, file path; remote rows also by harness). Enter keeps the search and also matches events; Esc clears it before Esc leaves the list.
- `r` on a row that resumes inside grok (Claude, Codex, grok) only arms it and says it can start a model turn; a second `r` resumes; any other key disarms. Pi, omp and Cursor rows copy their command on the first `r` as before.
- `y` copies the harness's own resume command (`cd <folder> && claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>`, `grok --resume <id>`, the Pi/omp/Cursor commands). Nothing runs.
- Follow's selected row uses grok's selection (`selection_overlay`: the theme's `bg_visual` band, reverse video in the bandless terminal theme) with bright bold text; tests check it against every shipped theme.

- `y` copies the harness's own resume command (`cd <folder> && claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>`, `grok --resume <id>`, the Pi/omp/Cursor commands). Nothing runs.

The standalone command opens the Traces list directly. Alternatively, run `grok-fork` and type `/traces` in the prompt.

## List keys (2026-11-11)

- `/` searches the list (title, folder, model, id, file path; remote rows also by harness). Enter keeps the search and also matches events; Esc clears it before Esc leaves the list.
- `r` on a row that resumes inside grok (Claude, Codex, grok) only arms it and says it can start a model turn; a second `r` resumes; any other key disarms. Pi, omp and Cursor rows copy their command on the first `r` as before.
- `y` copies the harness's own resume command (`cd <folder> && claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>`, `grok --resume <id>`, the Pi/omp/Cursor commands). Nothing runs.
- Follow's selected row uses grok's selection (`selection_overlay`: the theme's `bg_visual` band, reverse video in the bandless terminal theme) with bright bold text; tests check it against every shipped theme.

- `y` copies the harness's own resume command (`cd <folder> && claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>`, `grok --resume <id>`, the Pi/omp/Cursor commands). Nothing runs.
- Follow's selected row uses grok's selection (`selection_overlay`: the theme's `bg_visual` band, reverse video in the bandless terminal theme) with bright bold text; tests check it against every shipped theme.
